entity.description:
is a national park of the United States located in southwestern South Dakota. It protects 242,756 acres of sharply eroded buttes and pinnacles, as well as mixed grass prairie. Native Americans were once known to have roamed the land, with tribe managing the park along with the . Known native fauna are the American bison, the , the coyote, the , rattlesnakes, and the as examples.

Badlands National Park is also rich in fossil records. The oldest rocks were deposited 75 million years ago in the Western Interior Seaway, a shallow inland sea that stretched from the Gulf of Mexico to the Arctic Ocean. They belong to the Pierre Shale, which contains fossils of marine animals such as mosasaurs, plesiosaurs, and ammonites. However, the true speciality of the badlands is the from the Oligocene epoch, as they contain the richest deposits of Oligocene mammals known. Notable mammals include Archaeotherium, Hyaenodon, Subhyracodon, , , , oreodonts, and nimravids.

Badlands National Park is featured in the parks guide section of the now defunct Jurassic Park Institute.
